About Us
Benefits

At Swaralaya School of Music, we believe that music education should be both structured and inspiring. Our Music Grade Certification pathway is designed to help students set meaningful goals, stay motivated, and celebrate their achievements at every stage of their musical journey.
Why We Encourage Music Grade Exams

We actively encourage students to take up Music Grade Examinations as part of their learning journey.    Provides clear milestones for younger learners   Adds motivation and purpose for adult students   Helps track consistent progress and growth   Builds confidence through achievement
By working towards certifications, students develop discipline while enjoying the process of learning music.
Certification with Oriental Examination Board, London

Our students currently appear for examinations conducted by the Oriental Examination Board, London, a globally recognized institution.  The board offers: A structured Carnatic music syllabus Multiple graded levels for progressive learning Comprehensive evaluation through: Practical (Vocal Performance) Theory (Music Concepts)  This ensures a balanced development of both performance skills and theoretical understanding.
A Unique, Stress-Free Learning Method

Unlike traditional exam preparation methods, Swaralaya follows a holistic and stress-free approach.  Students are: Prepared intuitively during regular classes Not exposed to competitive pressure Encouraged to learn at their natural pace  This methodology has been thoughtfully designed by our Founder Director, Vandana Ram, and our dedicated teaching team is also well trained on the same.  Our goal is simple: Make learning joyful while achieving excellence.
Celebrating Achievements: Felicitation Ceremony
We recently hosted our Second Felicitation Ceremony, celebrating students who successfully cleared their music grade exams across various levels.
This event was a proud moment for: Students who achieved new milestones Parents who supported their journey Teachers who guided them every step of the way
Quarterly Exams & Recognition

To maintain momentum and motivation, Swaralaya aims to: Conduct Music Grade Exams quarterly Organize regular felicitation ceremonies Encourage continuous learning and progression  This consistent cycle of learning → certification → recognition keeps students engaged and inspired.
A Culture of Learning & Celebration

At Swaralaya School of Music, we go beyond teaching, we build a community of passionate learners.  Our approach ensures: Structured yet joyful learning Recognition of every achievement Encouragement without pressure or stress
Start Your Musical Journey Today
Whether you're a beginner or an experienced learner, Swaralaya School of Music provides the perfect platform to learn, grow, and excel in Carnatic music.

Swarakshara Annual Day 2025: The Heart of Swaralaya School of Music in the Netherlands

In the heart of the Netherlands, where diverse cultures blend seamlessly, music becomes a powerful medium of expression and connection. For students, parents, teachers, and organisers, an annual day represents the culmination of months of preparation, dedication, and shared experiences. At Swaralaya School of Music, this collective journey finds its expression in Swarakshara Annual Day, an event that reflects musical learning, emotional growth, confidence, and community spirit.

Swarakshara Annual Day is more than a stage performance. It is the annual representation of everything Swaralaya stands for: nurturing creativity, encouraging self-expression, and fostering a deep sense of belonging through music.
What Is Swarakshara Annual Day at Swaralaya?

Swarakshara is the annual day celebration of Swaralaya School of Music in the Netherlands. The name derives from two meaningful elements: “swar”, meaning musical notes, and “akshara”, meaning indestructible. Together, Swarakshara symbolises melodies that leave a lasting and meaningful impact on the hearts of students and audiences alike.

Held once every year, Swarakshara Annual Day brings together students of all age groups and skill levels to present what they have learned throughout the year. Rather than focusing on perfection, the event celebrates effort, growth, and sincere musical expression.
Swaralaya School of Music: The Foundation Behind Swarakshara

Located in Almere, Swaralaya School of Music offers structured training in Indian Carnatic music while embracing inclusivity and cultural exchange. Students from across the Netherlands participate through both in-person and online classes, making learning accessible and flexible.
The school’s philosophy centres on:
• Self-expression through music• Emotional well-being and confidence building• Cultural appreciation and inclusivity
These values directly shape Swarakshara Annual Day, ensuring that the celebration remains a reflection of Swaralaya’s educational and cultural ethos rather than a conventional performance event.
Swarakshara: The Annual Culmination of What Swaralaya Stands For

Annual day programmes often resemble an emotional rollercoaster filled with excitement, pride, anticipation, and nervous energy. From late-night practice sessions and last-minute costume adjustments to on-stage adaptations and backstage coordination, every participant contributes to the journey.

Swarakshara Annual Day represents the joyous annual celebration of the melody that lies within the students of Swaralaya School of Music in the Netherlands. While the performances are the most visible aspect, the true essence of Swarakshara lies in the collective effort behind the scenes.

Parents, teachers, students, administrators, and volunteers together create an atmosphere of togetherness that forms the backbone of Swaralaya. For those who experience Swarakshara firsthand, the event offers a deeper understanding of what Swaralaya truly represents as a community.
Music with Meaning: The Essence of Swarakshara Annual Day

Each song performed during Swarakshara Annual Day is carefully selected to create a lasting impact not only on the audience, but also on the students who learn and perform them. This enduring influence reflects the “akshara” aspect of Swarakshara, symbolising indestructible musical impressions.

Performances feature participants from diverse age groups, backgrounds, and skill levels, presenting a variety of musical pieces across genres rooted in Carnatic tradition. This inclusive approach reflects Swaralaya’s core belief: music is meant to soothe, inspire, and help individuals express themselves, rather than simply impress an audience.
Event Highlights of Swarakshara Annual Day
Swarakshara Annual Day offers a thoughtfully curated programme that showcases the depth and diversity of learning at Swaralaya.
Key highlights include:
• Student vocal performances across multiple learning levels• Accompaniment by experienced musicians• Integration of dance and visual elements• A supportive, encouraging performance environment
The emphasis remains on building confidence, stage presence, and emotional resilience, ensuring that students experience growth at every step.
Community Spirit at the Core of Swarakshara Annual Day

Community lies at the heart of Swaralaya School of Music, and this is most evident during Swarakshara Annual Day. The event brings together families, teachers, and well-wishers who share a common appreciation for music and culture.
For parents, Swarakshara offers:
• Moments of pride in witnessing their children perform• Reassurance that learning is about growth rather than comparison
For students, it provides:
• A safe and encouraging platform for self-expression• A strong sense of belonging and achievement
Benefits of Participating in Swarakshara Annual Day
Participation in Swarakshara Annual Day offers meaningful benefits that extend beyond the stage.
Students gain:
• Improved musical skills and discipline• Confidence through stage exposure• Emotional growth and self-expression
Families experience:
• Stronger community connections• Shared cultural and musical appreciation
These outcomes align with Swaralaya’s year-round commitment to holistic musical education.
Preparing for Swarakshara: A Supportive Journey

Preparation for Swarakshara Annual Day is carefully guided by teachers to ensure students feel supported throughout the process. Song selection, practice routines, and performance readiness are tailored to individual comfort levels.
The preparation journey focuses on:
• Enjoying the learning process• Managing stage anxiety through encouragement• Celebrating progress and effort at every stage
Looking Ahead: The Future of Swarakshara Annual Day

As Swaralaya School of Music continues to grow, Swarakshara Annual Day is poised to evolve further. With increasing participation and interest, the event may expand to reach more audiences across the Netherlands, while continuing to uphold its core values of expression, inclusivity, and community.
Conclusion: Discover the Melody That Lies Within

Swarakshara Annual Day encapsulates the spirit of Swaralaya School of Music in the Netherlands. It is not merely an annual showcase, but a reflection of what Swaralaya nurtures throughout the year, music that helps students express, soothe, inspire, and grow with confidence.
It brings to light, what Swaralaya helps students do:
"Discover the melody that lies within"

Celebrating 150 Years of Vande Mataram – The Almere Moment That Lit Up the Netherlands!
The Song That Still Gives Us Chills After 150 Years

“Vande Mataram” is more than a melody; it is a heartbeat for millions of Indians worldwide. Every Indian grows up with Vande Mataram running in their blood. Written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, it wasn’t just a poem, it was fire. Freedom fighters sang it in jails; kids whispered it in secret meetings, and today, 150 years later, it still makes the hair on the back of your neck stand up. In Almere, hearing those opening lines “Vande Mataram… Sujalam, Suphalam…” feels like a warm hug from home. And that’s exactly why this anniversary hit is different.
When the Indian Embassy Knocked on Our Door

Picture the scene: When the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, announced global celebrations for the 150-year milestone, the Embassy of India in The Hague reached out to Swaralaya School of Music, Almere, for a tribute.

Swaralaya School of Music is not just an Indian music school in the Netherlands. It is a vibrant community of learners, teachers, families and artists who celebrate Indian heritage through music every single day. Our school has woven Indian classical traditions into the cultural fabric of Almere, and this invitation recognized that commitment.
81 Voices. One Weekend. Infinite Passion.
Once the request came in, the answer was immediate YES!
In true Swaralaya spirit:
81 singers and instrumentalists stepped forward
rehearsals ran across two dedicated days, fueled by tea, snacks, laughter
filming took place during Almere’s breathtaking golden hour
our sound engineering team worked tirelessly to perfect every note
From beginners to advanced vocalists, from children discovering ragas to adults reclaiming their musical journey, everyone stood together to honour India’s priceless national song.
Watch the Official Vande Mataram Tribute Video
Swaralaya School of Music Almere students performing Vande Mataram tribute.
Almere Went Viral: A Moment That Stopped the Internet
When the Indian Embassy published the video on its official social platforms, something magical happened. The Netherlands paused to listen.
Within hours, comments poured in:
“My daughter is in this video!”
“Almere looks incredible, where was this filmed?”
“Dutch colleagues asked for a translation!”
“Proud of our community!”
The tribute quickly became one of the most watched posts ever shared by the Indian Mission in the Netherlands, reaching Indians, Dutch audiences, Surinamese families, and expats across Europe.
This was more than a video. It was a moment of unity.
Why This Tribute Mattered So Deeply
The beauty of this performance was not just in the music; it was in the togetherness.

It didn’t matter if someone was from Kerala, Punjab, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Suriname, or born here in the Netherlands. For those few minutes, we were one voice, one family, one song bridging cultures and generations.
Children gained confidence. Parents felt pride.
Swaralaya School of Music: Your Home for Indian Music in the Netherlands

Swaralaya School of Music has always believed in preserving and spreading Indian cultural heritage in the Netherlands through music, whether classical, devotional, light music or instrumental arts. This project reaffirmed that mission.
We continue to offer:
Indian classical vocal training.
Carnatic & Hindustani classes in Almere.
Instrumental lessons (Veena, Violin, Mridangam, Keyboard, Guitar & more)
Kids & teens music Batch.
Group singing sessions.
Join Swaralaya School of Music – Enrol, Learn & Shine
Whether you are:
A parent seeking cultural connections for their child.
A beginner hoping to start your musical journey.
A trained singer wishing to refine your skills.
An adult rediscovering Indian music after years.
Or someone who simply wants to be part of a passionate community.
Swaralaya welcomes you warmly.

Carnatic music made simple - 5 basic terms every beginner in Carnatic Music should know!

When coming across the term “Carnatic music” one might imagine an intricately designed pattern of notes, a grand performance with musicians having years of experience and practice, commanding the attention of the audience. Or maybe you think of the complicated yet intricate Ragas; evoking various emotions and creating a unique experience.To a beginner, Carnatic music tends to appear both incredibly awesome and also incrediblycomplicated at the same time.It can be easy to get lost in all the new terms, concepts, and nuances. One might even bediscouraged to pursue this journey in the first place!But here's the thing: music is for everyone. And we are here to make this journey a little biteasier for you. Let's get started!!

Shruthi - In simple terms; Shruthi is the pitch, or the reference point for your notes. One can imagine it as the Cricket Pitch from where the ball (notes) bounces. It is important to find the right pitch which feels comfortable for YOU to sing in.
Swara - Swara refers to the notes in Carnatic Music. The notes are; Shadjam, Rishabham, Gandharam, Madhyamam, Panchamam, Daivatam, Nishadam. It is also known as Sa, RI, GA, Ma, Pa, Da, Ni.

Swarasthanas - Remember the 7 notes? Now some of these notes have variations within them. You can think of them as different flavors of the same basic ingredient. Except Shadjam and Panchamam, known as Achala Swaras! Those two notes are like coconuts (you don't have different types of coconuts) but you DO have different kinds of mangoes; the rest of the notes are like that (Vikriti Swaras). In total, there are twelve unique sounds that can be produced in Carnatic Music. These are the 12 Swarasthanas. (We’ll get into their names in another blog post)
Tala - In Carnatic music, Tala is the rhythmic framework for the musical composition. One can think of it as a musical clock.
Raga - Raga is a musical framework used for improvisation. Each Raga has a specific set of notes and patterns. The Raga helps in setting the overall mood and evoking specific emotions.

So there we go; the 5 basic terms in Carnatic Music for beginners. Now the thing is, there are a LOT more terms, and a LOT more nuances to each of these terms. But, it is important to not let that deter you from your Carnatic music journey. After all, at theend of the day, this journey is about discovering the melody that ALREADY lies within you!! So go on, learn these terms, learn the context. But most importantly; Don't forget to have fun!
